title: Lowe’s and Dallas Cowboys honor Army veteran couple receiving Building Homes for Heroes’ 500th home
summary: Lowe’s and Dallas Cowboys honor Army veteran couple receiving Building Homes for Heroes’ 500th home
body_markdown:
Service for U.S. Army veterans Natalie and Brian Vines continued long after the uniforms were folded away.


With more than two decades of service each, and two tours in Iraq for Natalie, the couple found new purpose as advocates and volunteers, guiding fellow veterans through the challenges of recovery and the journey home.


Now, the community that has felt their impact is stepping forward in support.


Recently, Natalie and Brian stepped into the


Lowe’s of


Flower Mound, Texas, greeted by a Salute to Service celebration in their honor. Lowe’s associates, Building Homes for Heroes, and the Dallas Cowboys gathered to recognize the couple’s remarkable 50 years of military service, dedicating two permanent veteran parking spaces in their names as a lasting tribute.


“We’re really excited because we got to help Building Homes for Heroes and recognize an amazing veteran couple who


is


getting the 500th home built through Building Homes for Heroes,” said Tim Favis, Lowe’s district manager for North Dallas-Fort Worth. “Today we were just excited to be here at our Flower Mound store to dedicate two permanent parking spaces for both Brian and Natalie Vines.”
